When we compress air, as happens in a constriction, its stiffness
rises, so making a constriction at a place that experiences lots of
compression, will raise frequency. And bunching up air makes its
mas//density larger, so in a part of the vocal tract where air moves a
lot, constricting raises mass! So making a constriction increases
mass and increases stiffness.

But be careful!!!! This doesn’t mean that constrictions have no effect
on frequency!!! Why? Because the parts of a vibrating medium that
moves the most alternate with those that compress/uncompress
the most!

A purely linear network
2 inputs → hidden layers of 3, 2 and 4 neurons → 5 outputs. No activation functions.

The same network in PyTorch





                                                          /done/
                                                            import torch
                                                            import torch.nn as nn
                                                          /dune/

                                                            # purely linear: 2 → 3 → 2 → 4 → 5
                                                          /dean/      net = nn.Sequential(
                                                                nn.Linear(2, 3, bias=False),  # 2 in → 3 out
                                                          /Don/           nn.Linear(3, 2, bias=False),  # 3 in → 2 out
                                                                nn.Linear(2, 4, bias=False),  # 2 in → 4 out
                                                          /Dan/           nn.Linear(4, 5, bias=False),  # 4 in → 5 out
                                                            )  input · 2     hidden 1 · 3    hidden 2 · 2    hidden 3 · 4     output · 5


                                                                 Declaration only, no training. bias=False keeps every layer
